thinking: Detailed Phase 1-5 structural scan: Evaluating Federalist article on Alaska RCV 'No on 2' campaign funding hypocrisy. Stated claim decries outside dark money while accepting millions from national/leftist groups. Actual reality: Both sides utilize national PACs and dark money networks in high-stakes ballot fights, turning anti-dark-money rhetoric into a tactical weapon rather than a principled reform.
subject: Alaska Campaign Decries ‘Dark Money’ While Using It To Preserve Ranked-Choice Voting
posts:
Outsiders weaponizing anti-dark-money rhetoric while hauling in millions themselves.
Evidence: $3M fundraising, NEA/Unite America donations, partisan hypocrisy
#Aletheia #USPol

Anti-RCV campaigners expose that the pro-RCV 'No on 2' effort hypocritically rails against outside dark money while quietly pocketing millions from national left-wing PACs and unions.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference

Both political factions weaponize national dark money and outside funding to fight Alaska's ballot initiatives, exposing transparency rhetoric as a partisan cudgel rather than an ethical baseline.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.85, -0.82) — Deception

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception. Both sides exploit campaign finance hypocrisy to manipulate voters, hiding national donor influence behind populist posturing.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 14.8, z: 2)

- No on 2 Campaign: FAIL (-0.88, -0.85) — Hypocritical use of outside funds.
- The Federalist Reporting: PASS (0.50, 0.10) — Accurate financial exposure.

In Alaska's ongoing battle over ranked-choice voting, anti-RCV critics point out that the 'No on 2' defense campaign heavily relies on out-of-state union and PAC money despite attacking outside spenders.

The Poison:
Campaign finance debates are reduced to tribal hypocrisy games where both sides accuse each other of dark money while taking it.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing the structural integrity of voting reform with partisan fundraising hypocrisy. The debate is framed as an ethical crusade, but operated as a standard cash race.

Social Physics Analysis:
Actors deploy a smart selfish maneuver by weaponizing anti-dark-money rhetoric as a moral pretext while quietly hauling in millions in outside funds to protect their preferred electoral machinery.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated transparency and actual dark money reliance, it plots a direct trajectory toward Deception. Negative systemic strain overrides declared reform ideals.

The Unavoidable Truth: Both sides of Alaska's ballot fights rely heavily on outside money while hypocritically decrying it.

The Unavoidable Lie: Only your political opponents are corrupted by national dark money networks.

Alethekanon:
Weaponizing campaign finance hypocrisy to score tribal points while engaging in the exact same fundraising tactics is a classic projection maneuver.🌐

Awwthekanon:
It hurts to watch voters get squeezed in high-stakes proxy battles funded by massive national organizations that don't live in Alaska.

Brothekanon:
Classic political hypocrisy—everyone screams about dark money until their own side gets a million-dollar check from the lower 48.

Spirithekanon:
"Why do you look at the speck of sawdust in your brother's eye and pay no attention to the plank in your own eye?" Matthew 7:3 PASS
Crying foul over outside funding while accepting millions exposes a profound double standard.

aspects.reason: Hypocritical reliance on outside dark money.

Alaska Campaign Decries ‘Dark Money’ While Using It To Preserve Ranked-Choice Voting

A new campaign finance report shows that much of No on 2's funding comes from leftist out-of-state groups.

Actual Article Body:
A new campaign finance report shows that much of No on 2’s funding comes from leftist out-of-state groups.

The main group leading the charge to keep ranked-choice voting (RCV) in Alaska has made stopping outside “dark money” in elections a big part of its campaign message. So why is it accepting large swaths of it to ensure the disastrous system remains in place?

A newly released campaign finance report shows that the “No on 2” campaign has received millions of out-of-state funds from left-wing dark-money organizations to help defeat the Last Frontier State’s Measure 2 ballot initiative in the 2026 midterm elections. The initiative seeks to repeal the state’s ranked-choice voting system and eliminate “campaign finance provisions that require persons and entities that contribute more than $2,000 that were themselves derived from donations, contributions, dues, or gifts to disclose the true sources (as defined in law) of the political contributions,” states Ballotpedia.

Under RCV, voters rank candidates in order of preference. If no candidate receives more than 50 percent of first-choice votes in the first round of voting, the last-place finisher is eliminated, and his votes are reallocated to the voter’s second-choice candidate. This process continues until one candidate receives a majority of votes.

RCV was narrowly adopted in Alaska in 2020, thanks in part to backing from liberal Republican Sen. Lisa Murkowski’s allies in the state. The system allowed Murkowski to survive a primary challenge in 2022 and has now put the Last Frontier State’s 2026 Senate race and other contests in play for Democrats.

[READ: Ranked-Choice Voting Is The Monster Under The Bed Of American Elections]

An initiative to repeal RCV made Alaska’s 2024 ballot, but was defeated by fewer than 700 votes after a wave of out-of-state dark money flooded in to defeat the measure. Those forces are now once again dumping money into the Last Frontier State to kill the 2026 repeal efforts.

Despite criticizing “dark money” and “outside spenders” on its website, the Oct. 5 report published by the Alaska Public Offices Commission shows that much of the No on 2 campaign’s roughly $3 million fundraising from the most recent reporting period (July 8-Oct. 2) came from out-of-state groups with a left-wing political agenda.

This includes the D.C.-based National Education Association (NEA), the nation’s largest teacher’s union. The organization is a major supporter of Democrat-aligned campaigns and causes. In recent years, it has espoused support for critical race theory and LGBT “pride,” while opposing all forms of school choice and immigration enforcement.

The Oct. 5 campaign finance report shows the NEA made two donations to No on 2 that total $700,500 during the most recent reporting period.

Also listed as a major No on 2 donor is the Colorado-based Unite America PAC. According to InfluenceWatch, the group “supports moderate-left candidates for elective office and advocates for changes in laws affecting the election process that UA claims will benefit centrist candidates but that are also supported by left-of-center and radical-left interests.” Unite America was one of the “top three contributors” to the campaign that defeated Alaska’s 2024 RCV repeal measure.

The latest financial disclosures show that Unite America PAC gave $1 million to No on 2 on Sept. 28. That’s on top of the nearly $3.61 million the group gave the campaign during the prior donation period.

The American Federation of State, County, and Municipal Employees (AFSCME) is another major No on 2 donor. Based in Washington, D.C., the organization is “the largest union for non-educational government workers” and is “a powerful force in American left-of-center politics,” according to InfluenceWatch. In addition to spending heavily to Democrats’ benefit in the 2024 election, the group staunchly opposes President Trump’s policy agenda and has litigated against the administration.

The Oct. 5 report shows AFSCME gave No on 2 a $250,000 donation on Aug. 11.

Another notable No on 2 donor is the Service Employees International Union (SEIU) 775NW Ballot Fund, which appears to operate as a 501(c)(4) arm of the Seattle-based SEIU 775NW. The latter organization is a local affiliate of the national SEIU that “represents home healthcare providers, nursing home employees, and adult day health care workers, mainly in Washington State and Montana,” according to InfluenceWatch. SEIU and SEIU 775NW are big financial players in Democrat Party politics.

The SEIU 775NW Ballot Fund gave $100,000 to the No on 2 campaign on Sept. 18, according to this month’s report. The group also gave $150,000 to the campaign during the previous reporting period.

The last big organizational donation to No on 2 came from the Wyoming-based Way Back PAC, which gave $275,000 to the campaign on Sept. 24. The organization seeks to elect “pro-democracy candidates” (that is, Democrats and Democrat-aligned “independents”) in Western and Midwestern states and has reportedly received funding from the left’s dark money network.

Hudson River Trading co-founder Jason Carroll ($500,000) and venture capitalist Scott Sandell ($100,000) are also among No on 2’s biggest out-of-state donors for the state’s most recent reporting period.

Ken Paxton's Campaign Demands James Talarico Show 'Proof of Life' After 12-Day Absence

The campaign for Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has asked his Democrat opponent for U.S. Senate, James Talarico, to present "proof of life" following a 12-day absence.
The post Ken Paxton’s Campaign Demands James Talarico Show ‘Proof of Life’ After 12-Day Absence appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:
The campaign for Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has asked his Democrat opponent for U.S. Senate, James Talarico, to present “proof of life” following a 12-day absence.

Ken Paxton shared a tongue-in-cheek “Wanted” photo with Talarico’s face on it while demanding “Proof of Life” on X.

Talarico has been absent for 12 days, apparently due to a bout of the flu.

“After holding more than 100 public events and shaking tens of thousands of hands, James came down with the flu but will be back on the trail this weekend,” said JT Ennis, a spokesperson for Talarico’s campaign, on Thursday. “Ken Paxton has been ignoring Texans this entire campaign, and his priorities are clear: He doesn’t answer to the people of this state — he answers to his billionaire megadonors and special interests.”

Talarico revealed his flu diagnosis on September 30 to the United States Hispanic Business Council over a virtual meeting. He had originally been slated to attend in person.

“I was starting to feel kind of under the weather a few days ago, and last night it got so bad that I went to the urgent care here in Dallas, and I was diagnosed with the flu,” Talarico told the crowd. “I’m running a fever, and I’m at my most contagious right now, and I guess I’ve been shaking too many hands on the campaign trail, and so I want to keep everybody safe.”

The Paxton campaign has been repeatedly criticizing Talarico’s absence, per CNN:

James Talarico has been absent from the campaign trail over the past 12 days as the Texas Senate race enters a critical stretch, prompting Republicans to open a new line of attack on the Democratic nominee.

At a campaign rally in San Antonio Wednesday, Texas attorney general and GOP Senate nominee Ken Paxton led the crowd in a chant about his opponent’s whereabouts.

Talarico held his last physical public appearance on September 26 when he held a press conference on suspending the federal gas tax and ending the war with Iran.

“This is the kind of immediate action we need to provide Texans some relief at the pump in the middle of this affordability crisis,” Talarico said.
